To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the evaluation methodology developed for XML retrieval is based on the evaluation of the effectiveness of information access, and that the evaluation of XML retrieval requires an appropriate definition of relevance and the use of appropriate metrics.

(1) the evaluation methodology developed for INEX is sound, as it has been shown to be consistent with the evaluation criteria, (2) the evaluation methodology can be successfully used in the evaluation of XML retrieval systems, (3) it is possible to evaluate XML retrieval systems in an effective way and (4) the evaluation methodology is extensible to other retrieval tasks.

1) the evaluation of XML retrieval is not a trivial extension of IR evaluation; 2) the evaluation of structural similarity between queries and documents is not trivial, and 3) the notion of relevance is not trivial in an XML context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is an appropriate notion of relevance for XML retrieval?

how the notion of relevance can be extended and adapted to take into account the structure of XML documents, how the relevance of a retrieval result can be assessed in a way that is sensitive to the structural aspects of the XML document and how this relevance assessment can be used in the context of evaluation.
the following questions: (i) what is the most appropriate way of scoring XML retrieval?;
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the INEX evaluation methodology is sound and has proven its worth.
, in INEX, we have tried to develop an evaluation framework that is as close as possible to that of the TREC conference, but that also allows for the evaluation of XML retrieval systems.
the INEX evaluation methodology is the most advanced and complete one for evaluating XML retrieval systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
INEX has shown that XML retrieval is a challenging research area and that there are a number of issues that still require investigation.
we have been able to establish a methodology for XML retrieval evaluation which is now widely adopted.
INEX has been successful in establishing a community of researchers in XML retrieval, and in developing a methodology for evaluating XML retrieval.
The main takeaway from our work is that

evaluation of XML retrieval systems requires the development of a specific methodology that takes into account the peculiarities of the XML format, such as the fact that documents are composed of several components, which may be of different types and levels of granularity, and that they may be nested.
the evaluation of XML retrieval is not only a matter of adapting traditional metrics to a new context, but rather of developing new metrics and new paradigms.

the evaluation of XML retrieval systems is not a straightforward extension of the evaluation of IR systems and that the evaluation paradigm needs to be adapted to take into account the specificities of XML documents.
